bull_bear.body:
- "Well capitalized 21.3% CRAR, with strong ALM and access to diversified sources of funds"; standalone CRAR shown at 21.3% for FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27, down from 30.9% in FY25.
- Consolidated net worth of Rs 16,552 Cr and BVPS of Rs 176.2 in Q1 FY27; consolidated borrowings of Rs 60,171 Cr against total assets of Rs 77,990 Cr.
- Consolidated funding mix in Q1 FY27: Term Loan 45.6%, ECB and USD Bond 20.7%, WCDL/CC 17.1%, NCD 9.0%, Commercial Paper 7.4%, Securitization 0.2%.
- Ratings cited: CRISIL AA (Stable) long term and A1+ short term domestically, BB-/Stable from S&P and Fitch internationally, CRISIL AA- for Asirvad and the HFC; a $300 mn Reg S debt raise in May 2024 is noted.
- Asirvad capital adequacy rose to 31.0% in Q1 FY27 from 20.2% in FY26; the deck states no dividend or buyback policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Core claim is operational rigor in gold lending — "Perfected the art of managing appraisal, custodial and valuation risks that are inherent in gold lending" — plus trusted-brand safekeeping of household gold jewellery for 2.9 mn active customers.
- "Pioneer in process innovation in gold loans (online gold loan product 'OGL' and cellular vaulting mechanism)"; stated as the first NBFC to launch OGL, in September 2015.
- Stated growth strategy is to "Create market for gold loans as a mainstream, convenient and affordable product" and be a "One stop shop for meeting customers borrowing and protection needs (small ticket loans to underbanked customers)".
- Non-gold is explicitly a "Calibrated approach to growth in other loan products - MFI, home loans, loans against property and MSME", alongside prudent credit and risk management including "timely auctions".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Asirvad underwriting] Borrower-overlap discipline: clients with up to 3 lenders improved to 95.2% in Jun'26 from 93.8% in Mar'26 and 85.4% in Sep'25, versus an industry figure of 98.0%; clients with exposure >= Rs 2 lakhs fell to 5.7% from 6.1% in March 2026 and 7.9% in Sep 2025, "mainly due to closure of old pool customers".
- [Asirvad old vs new book] The MFI book is split into an old book (customers down to 7.6 lakh from 18.8 lakh YoY; Stage 3 of Rs 301 Cr on a Rs 1,293 Cr book) and a fast-growing new book (customers up to 6.8 lakh from 0.9 lakh; Stage 3 of Rs 10 Cr on a Rs 3,274 Cr book).
- [Group structure] Subsidiaries listed are Manappuram Home Finance Limited, Manappuram Insurance Broker Limited, Asirvad Microfinance Limited and Manappuram Comptech and Consultants Limited, with holdings printed as 100%, 100%, 98.97% and 99.81%; the entity-to-percentage binding is not explicit in the extract.
- [Board] Two Bain Capital partners sit on the Board as Non-Executive, Non-Independent Directors (Rishi Mandawat and Ashish Kotecha); the Chairman & Managing Director is V.P. Nandakumar and Dr. Sumitha Nandan is Executive Director & Vice-Chairperson.
- [Shareholding] Shareholding pattern as on 30 June 2026 is printed as Promoters 42%, FPI 22%, Mutual Funds 14%, Financial Institution/Banks/Insurance 4%, Non-Institutions 18%; largest non-promoter holder listed is Small World Fund INC at 5.49%.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Manappuram as a "Leading gold loan player in India, with a trusted brand and nation-wide reach", a pioneer in gold-loan process innovation (Online Gold Loan and cellular vaulting), pursuing a "calibrated approach to growth" in non-gold products to become "the financial partner of choice to under-banked customers across their lifecycle".

open.item: Standalone cost of borrowing expected to move to ~9.3%; margins to remain stable.
Focus on secured lending in non-gold verticals; reduce unsecured MSME share (~5%) further toward 2-3%.
Flagged MFI collection stress in Punjab, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat from floods, heat waves, elections and loan-waiver rumours.
Asirvad IPO progressing with roadshow started; SEBI approval received, delay attributed to elections not CEO vacancy.
Cost rationalization in gold loan business; additional business over fixed branch setup to reduce opex.
Auction surplus reduced to ~INR14 cr (from INR48 cr), falling ~INR2 cr/quarter; expects RBI branch permission.
Applied for 300 new gold loan branches; expects RBI permission after reducing auction surplus.
Expect RBI permission for new gold loan branches after demonstrating auction surplus reduction.

verdicts.item: Maintain gold loan pricing/yield discipline at around 22% plus in a competitive environment.
verdicts.note: 'net yields on the gold loan portfolio has also come down from 22.5% to 22.2%' - still above the ~22% discipline threshold.

verdicts.item: Expect gold loan AUM growth of ~8-10% YoY in the coming quarters despite pricing discipline.
verdicts.note: 'Our gold AUM reached INR23,647 crores, an improvement of 14.8% over the same quarter last year and 10% sequentially' - beat the 8-10% band.

verdicts.item: Preparing Asirvad for IPO; Manappuram promoters not participating in any pre-IPO capital investment.
verdicts.note: 'the IPO is in progress', 'SEBI has given an approval' and 'we have started the road show' - Asirvad IPO preparation ongoing as committed.

verdicts.item: Focus on the affordable housing segment, seen as having significant potential.
verdicts.note: 'We are closely monitoring the affordable housing segment. It has significant potential' and home loan AUM 'INR1,587 crores ... 32% increase' - focus reaffirmed with growth.

verdicts.item: Expanding non-gold secured products (MSME, vehicle) beyond the current ~20% of gold loan branches used.
verdicts.note: 'These businesses are colocated along with the gold loan business ... done by separate teams' and non-gold at 47% of portfolio - expansion continuing but no branch-utilisation figure beyond ~20% confi…

verdicts.item: Flagged MFI stress in Punjab and Rajasthan; strengthened collection machinery, expects improvement in coming quarters.
verdicts.note: Expected improvement did not materialise: collection challenges continued across Punjab, Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP with 'INR71 crores write-off' and rising provisioning in Q1FY25.

verdicts.item: Maintain vehicle finance GNPA below 3% going forward.
verdicts.note: 'The GNPA stands at 3.6%' for Vehicle Finance - above the below-3% commitment.

verdicts.item: MFI credit cost expected to decline in coming quarters as collections strengthen week-on-week.
verdicts.note: 'provisioning for bad assets has been increasing consistently' and 'INR71 crores write-off' - MFI credit cost rose rather than declined.

verdicts.item: Net interest margin may dip slightly in FY25 but will be overcome by better growth; ROE target unaffected.
verdicts.note: 'margins at least should remain stable now? - Yes' and strong gold growth, but consolidated ROE at 19% is slightly below the 20% target.

verdicts.item: Expect robust gold loan growth in FY25, potentially better than FY24.
verdicts.note: 'gold AUM ... 14.8% over the same quarter last year' (vs 8.9% in Q4FY24) and 'somewhere around 15-plus percentage growth this year' - robust and better than FY24.

verdicts.item: Target ~20% AUM CAGR and sustainable ~20% consolidated ROE.
verdicts.note: 'consolidated AUM ... 21.2% Y-o-Y growth' meets the ~20% CAGR, but 'ROE on a consolidated basis was 19 percentage' - just short of the sustainable 20% ROE. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Asirvad Microfinance IPO expected without much delay per bankers' indication.
verdicts.note: 'SEBI has given an approval, but there has been a significant delay in getting the company listed' - management cites general elections/uncertainty; timeline pushed out, contrary to 'without much dela…

wtt.summary: 68% guidance hit (14 chains); 1 expired; 26% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Optimistic on gold loan demand recovery; management repeatedly deferred on Asirvad specifics citing DRHP, and candidly acknowledged sector-wide MFI and non-gold NPA stress while guiding to improvement from Q2.
